chunks: Abu al-Husayn ibn Abi Jeed informed me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If a man has remaining days of fasting from the month of Ramadan, let him make them up in whichever month he wishes, as consecutive days. If he is unable [to fast consecutively], let him make them up however he wishes, and let him specify the days. If he separates them, it is good; and if he continues them, it is good. I said: What do you think if there remains upon him something from the fasting of the month of Ramadan, should he make it up in Dhu al-Hijjah? He said: Yes.

key_terms.صَوْمُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Fasting of the month of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for making up missed Ramadan fasts regarding timing and consecutiveness?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies the flexibility in Qada fasting, emphasizing that while consecutive days are preferred, they are not obligatory, thereby alleviating hardship for the believer. It specifically addresses the common concern regarding fasting in Dhu al-Hijjah, confirming its permissibility for making up Ramadan fasts despite the general preference for avoiding voluntary fasting during this sacred month. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of balancing ritual obligation with ease (taysir).
